concepts.title: Definition of Inequalities
concepts.definition: A mathematical statement that compares two numerical values or algebraic expressions using order symbols like less than, greater than, or their inclusive counterparts.
concepts.formula: a < b, a > b, a <= b, a >= b
concepts.key_idea: Inequalities represent ranges or constraints rather than fixed equality.
question_patterns: identify if the statement is an inequality
differentiate between strict and slack inequalities
write an inequality for the given condition
what is a literal inequality
Explain the method of Definition of Inequalities.

solution_steps.explain: Check if the expression uses <, >, <=, or >=.
If it uses < or >, it is strict; if it uses <= or >=, it is slack.
Confirm that the two sides of the inequality are correctly ordered and that the comparison symbol matches the stated condition.

compute_steps.action: transpose the terms and divide by the coefficient
compute_steps.explain: transpose the terms and divide by the coefficient: x = (62 - 6) / 8 gives 7

concepts.title: Rules for Solving Inequalities
concepts.definition: Fundamental operations allowed on inequalities: adding/subtracting any number, and multiplying/dividing by positive numbers preserves the sign, while multiplying/dividing by negative numbers reverses it.
concepts.formula: if a < b and c < 0, then ac > bc
concepts.key_idea: The inequality sign flips only when multiplying or dividing by a negative value.
question_patterns: what happens when you multiply an inequality by a negative number
state the rules for solving linear inequalities
apply Rule 2 to solve the expression
why does the sign reverse in inequalities
Explain the method of Rules for Solving Inequalities.

solution_steps.explain: Add or subtract the same number on both sides without changing the sign.
If the multiplier is positive, keep the sign; if negative, reverse the sign.
Check the resulting inequality by substituting a test value to confirm the direction of the inequality sign is correct.

compute_steps.action: transpose the terms and divide by the coefficient
compute_steps.explain: transpose the terms and divide by the coefficient: x = (40 - 10) / 6 gives 5

concepts.title: Algebraic Solution of Linear Inequality in One Variable
concepts.definition: Finding the set of all real numbers, integers, or natural numbers that satisfy a linear inequality by isolating the variable.
concepts.formula: ax + b < c => x < (c - b) / a
concepts.key_idea: Isolate the variable x using inverse operations while respecting the sign reversal rule.
question_patterns: solve the inequality for x
find the solution set for natural numbers
calculate the value of x for which the expression is true
solve 30x < 200 when x is an integer
Explain the method of Algebraic Solution of Linear Inequality in One Variable.

solution_steps.explain: Subtract the constant b from both sides.
Divide by the coefficient a. Note: if a is negative, reverse the inequality sign.
Write the solution as an interval or set, restricting to the required domain such as natural numbers or integers if specified.

concepts.key_idea: The sum of all scores divided by the number of exams must meet or exceed the target average.

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the target average by the total number of examinations.
Add up the marks obtained in previous exams.
Subtract the current sum from the required total sum.

concepts.title: Solving Double Inequalities
concepts.definition: Solving expressions where a variable term is bounded between two values simultaneously.
concepts.key_idea: Perform the same operations on all three parts of the inequality to isolate the variable in the middle.

Subtract the constant b from the right bound.
Divide all parts by the coefficient a to find the range of x.
Divide the right adjusted bound by a.

concepts.title: Mixture Concentration Bounds
concepts.definition: Calculating the volume of a solution of a certain concentration that must be added to an existing solution to reach a target concentration range.
concepts.key_idea: The total acid content in the final mixture is the sum of acid in the individual components.

Explain the method of Mixture Concentration Bounds.

solution_steps.explain: Multiply existing volume by the difference between target and current concentration.
Find the difference between the added solution concentration and the target concentration.
Divide the numerator by the denominator to find the threshold volume.
